how_new_controls_are_frozen_without_fork.problem: PF2 requires seven controls that the batch manifest does not contain — the status-input refusal, the unarchive refusal, the aggregate-page refusal, the role-enforcement-layer refusal, the entrypoint derived-total reconciliation and the two mutations that make the first and the fourth non-vacuous. They must be frozen somewhere, and the batch manifest is integrated and immutable.
how_new_controls_are_frozen_without_fork.resolution: They are frozen in THIS artifact, under the reserved prefix PF2-, in the PF2_NEW_CONTROLS block. The batch manifest remains the sole contract for every id it defines; this authority defines only strictly-new ids and redefines none.
how_new_controls_are_frozen_without_fork.measured_disjointness_proof: The batch manifest contains 55 control and sentinel ids in exactly four prefixes — POS (16), NEG (24), MUT (12), SENT (3) — enumerated over positive_controls, negative_controls, mutation_controls and sentinels, with zero duplicates. Zero of those 55 ids begin with 'PF2-'. A repository-wide `grep -o 'PF2-[A-Z0-9-]*' -r docs/` returns no match at AS_OF_TREE, so the PF2- namespace is free in the whole of docs/, not merely in the batch manifest.
how_new_controls_are_frozen_without_fork.why_this_is_not_a_second_manifest: A second manifest would restate the batch manifest's PF2-scoped ids under a new manifest_id, creating two documents that both claim authority over POS-COMP-1 and its siblings. This artifact restates none of them: it CITES them by id as inherited and binding, and adds seven ids that exist nowhere else.

PARENT_AUTHORITY.relationship: SUCCESSOR. This artifact does not supersede, refine or correct any parent. It consumes the parent's already-frozen product decisions and converts the parent's frozen future implementation surface for PF2 — and only PF2 — into explicit write permission.

PURPOSE: Materialize the minimum append-only execution authority needed to convert the already-integrated PF2 frozen future surface into explicit write permission. The parent product authority carries PORTFOLIO_IMPLEMENTATION_AUTHORIZED = false and a null GRANT_ID: it froze WHAT may eventually be written and WHERE, and granted no permission to write it. PF1's successor supplied that permission for PF1 alone and has been implemented and integrated. This successor supplies it for PF2 alone — Portfolio composition, lifecycle and permissions — once independently audited, integrated, and once the two implementation preconditions recorded under LOCKS are released. It authorizes no implementation now.

SOURCE_CONSUMPTION.role: Zero-discovery input. SOURCE_CONSUMPTION.prohibition_honoured: The packet's instruction 'Independently derive exact future write surface from live authority' and 'Do not invent filenames' are both discharged structurally: PF2_WRITE_SURFACE is identical, path for path and in order, to the parent's authorized_future_implementation_surface.PF2_composition_and_permissions, and every path in it was existence-checked against AS_OF_TREE.

NO_PRODUCT_DECISION_REOPENED.method: Each obligation this authority states was checked against the parent's permissions, composition_contract, portfolio_cardinality, portfolio_size_contract and authorized_future_implementation_surface keys, and against a targeted occurrence count over the parent artifact for the terms that would signal a competing decision. A decision is REOPENED only if the parent states X and this artifact states not-X. A decision is INHERITED if the parent states X and this artifact restates X. A decision is an ADDITIVE GAP-FILL if the parent is silent on the question and this artifact answers it without contradicting anything the parent does state.

PF2_SEMANTICS_FROZEN.scope_statement: PF2 owns Portfolio composition, Portfolio lifecycle, Portfolio permissions, project assignment, unassignment and move, and archive semantics. It owns nothing else.

create.behaviour: Insert into portfolios with organization_id = the request scope, name required, description optional, status 'active', created_by = the caller.
create.status_input: REFUSED. The caller may not supply status on this path; see STATUS_INPUT_CONTRACT.
create.audit_verb: portfolio.created — EXISTS at lib/audit/logger.ts:154 as AUDIT_ACTIONS.PORTFOLIO_CREATED. PF2 adds no constant for it.

update.behaviour: Update name and/or description of a portfolio in the caller's organization.
update.status_input: REFUSED. Status is not updatable through this path, and the input surface may not accept it.

archive.behaviour: Set status='archived'. The archived portfolio remains readable, keeps its aggregate, and is READ-ONLY for composition: assign, unassign and move all refuse against it.
archive.grouping_only: Archiving a Portfolio MUST NOT archive its member projects, MUST NOT delete them, MUST NOT detach them (portfolio_id is not nulled), and MUST NOT alter any project evidence or any other Measure object. A portfolio is a grouping construct and never an ownership transfer (RE_U4 ownership_vs_access, PRESERVED). The write touches exactly one column of exactly one portfolios row.
archive.unarchive: OUT OF SCOPE for V1. Not authorized, and no path may perform it implicitly; see STATUS_INPUT_CONTRACT.

assign_project.precondition: The project and the portfolio both belong to the request-scope organization, verified in the same transaction as the write. The portfolio is not archived.
assign_project.behaviour: UPDATE projects SET portfolio_id = <portfolio> WHERE id = <project> AND organization_id = <scope> AND portfolio_id IS NULL
assign_project.same_organization_only: Non-waivable. A project in another organization may never be assigned, and the refusal is an application-layer refusal that RLS independently corroborates on the organization axis.

unassign_project.behaviour: UPDATE projects SET portfolio_id = NULL WHERE id = <project> AND organization_id = <scope> AND portfolio_id = <portfolio>
unassign_project.project_intact: The project remains fully intact; only the grouping is removed. No project status change, no soft delete, no evidence change.

move_project.decision: ONE HUMAN DECISION, ONE UPDATE. Not an unassign followed by an assign.
move_project.behaviour: UPDATE projects SET portfolio_id = <target> WHERE id = <project> AND organization_id = <scope> AND portfolio_id = <source>, with both portfolios verified to be in the scope organization and the target not archived.
move_project.no_partial_move: Zero rows updated means the source no longer matched. The operation is REFUSED — never retried, never silently converted into an assign, and never followed by a compensating write. There is no state in which the project belongs to no portfolio, so no concurrent aggregate read can observe a state no one chose.
move_project.audit_verb: project.portfolio_moved — NEW, carrying both endpoints in beforeJson and afterJson.
move_project.audit_row_count: EXACTLY ONE per move. Two rows for one move is the defect MUT-COMP-1 exists to catch.

permissions.read: viewer and above. Reviewer and viewer are read-only: no create, no update, no archive, no composition.
permissions.manage_composition: canManagePortfolio(role) = hasRole(role, 'impact_manager'), resolving to super_admin, organization_admin and impact_manager — the exact parent-authority role, restated without widening.
permissions.analyst: EXCLUDED from every composition capability. This is the parent's adjudicated narrowing of current behaviour and it is not softened here. Analyst gains no composition-management capability, and no implementation may grant it on the strength of the live inline arrays, which admit analyst today.
permissions.no_inline_role_arrays: After implementation, no inline role array may survive on any Portfolio path. The three live sites are lib/portfolios/service.ts:41, app/app/portfolios/page.tsx:22 and app/app/portfolios/new/page.tsx:17-19; all three carry the identical four-element array including 'analyst'. Every gate consults canManagePortfolio.

pagination_and_aggregate.page_membership_may_be_paginated: Permitted, not required, and not implemented by PF2 — see PAGINATION_DISPOSITION. Nothing in this authority obliges PF2 to paginate.
pagination_and_aggregate.aggregate_covers_all_members: Non-waivable and inherited verbatim: the authoritative aggregate is ALWAYS computed over every member project of the portfolio, never over the current page, and projectCount, includedCount and the excluded list continue to describe the WHOLE portfolio on every page.
pagination_and_aggregate.no_artificial_hard_denial: PF2 may not introduce a hard maximum on portfolio membership and may not refuse a write on member count. PORTFOLIO_SOFT_SIZE_THRESHOLD = 250 gates an informational notice and refuses nothing; treating it as a cap is a product refusal invented to simplify an implementation, which the parent forbids.

MUTATION_CONTRACT.non_vacuity_definition: A mutation control is non-vacuous only if applying the mutation to the real working tree makes at least one NAMED control fail, and if that control passes on the unmutated tree. A mutation that leaves the suite green proves the guarded assertion does not exist, and is itself a BLOCKING finding for the implementation node.

execution_obligations.real_bytes: Each mutation MUST be applied to real working-tree bytes and then restored byte-exactly. A mutation reasoned about but never applied does not discharge its control.
execution_obligations.pristine_capture_ordering: Capture the pristine copy of every file to be mutated BEFORE the first edit of the sequence, never inside the edit loop. Capturing a pristine copy after an earlier mutation has landed poisons the restore baseline and makes byte-exact restoration unverifiable.
execution_obligations.restoration_proof: Restoration is proven by hashing each mutated file before the first edit and after the final restore and comparing the two digests, and by confirming a clean `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` at the end of the mutation sequence. A visual re-read is not proof.
execution_obligations.chunking: The mutation sequence MUST be chunked so that no single command invocation can be interrupted mid-control. An interrupted run can leave a mutation on disk, which silently converts the working tree into a mutated tree for every subsequent gate.
execution_obligations.crlf_hazard: Every path in PF2's write surface is CRLF in the working tree — .gitattributes pins only docs/**, db/baseline/**, db/prepared/** and *.sh to LF. A mutation anchored on a bare newline will match nothing and the control will pass VACUOUSLY, reported as a false PASS. Anchor on \r?\n and confirm the occurrence count changed.
execution_obligations.scope: Mutations may touch only the thirteen authorized paths. A mutation that would require editing a fourteenth path is out of scope and its control must be redesigned within the thirteen.

EXECUTION_AUTHORIZATION.scope_of_the_grant: Write permission for the thirteen paths in PF2_WRITE_SURFACE, and for nothing else. The grant does not extend to PF1's or PF3's path sets, does not extend to any protected surface, and does not authorize a migration, a schema change, an RLS policy change, an ODS artifact or a Controller enumeration.
what_this_authority_does_not_do: It does not implement PF2. The working tree's PF2 paths are unchanged by this mission.
It does not authorize PF3, which requires its own successor.
It does not release either lock, and it does not amend the parent to widen PF2's surface.
It does not close the Portfolio tenancy coupling successor.
It does not edit, supersede or amend any parent or sibling artifact.

MEASURED_BASELINE_OF_THE_IMPLEMENTATION_.purpose: Record the live pre-PF2 state of the composition surface at AS_OF_TREE, so that an audit of the PF2 implementation node can distinguish what PF2 changed from what it inherited, and so that the mutation controls' non-vacuity claims are checkable against a fixed baseline.

measured_facts.fact: Exports exactly three functions: listPortfoliosForCurrentOrganization, getPortfolioByIdForCurrentOrganization and createPortfolioForCurrentOrganization. There is NO update path, NO archive path and NO composition path of any kind.
An inline role array ['super_admin','organization_admin','impact_manager','analyst'] gates create. It admits analyst, which the parent's adjudication removes.
PortfolioInputSchema accepts status as a two-value enum defaulting to 'active', and the insert writes data.status through. Creating directly into 'archived' is reachable from the exported function.
listProjectsForPortfolio(portfolioId) returns every member project, organization-bound, with no limit and no offset.

The same-organization verification precedent the parent cites: a portfolio reference supplied at project creation is checked against the caller's organization before the insert. This is the only place projects.portfolio_id is ever written today — at :90, on INSERT. No UPDATE of that column exists anywhere in lib/ or app/.

Twenty-three exported functions: hasRole at :24 (the ROLE_HIERARCHY comparator) and twenty-two discrete permission helpers built on it, plus the set-inclusion STELLA_ROLES constant at :104-110. canCreateProject requires impact_manager at :62-64. canManagePortfolio does NOT exist.
The AUDIT_ACTIONS object literal carries 104 entries and exactly one Portfolio verb, PORTFOLIO_CREATED = 'portfolio.created'. PF2's five new values occur nowhere in the file.

Both carry the identical inline four-role array including analyst. app/app/portfolios/[portfolioId]/page.tsx carries no role gate at all — it renders read-only content, so PF2 adds the first composition gate to it.

An inline 'use server' action handleCreate already exists inside the page and is covered by the page's own inventory row. It is a precedent for inline actions and is NOT a precedent for skipping the actions module PF2 must create.
checkedModules 143, databaseReaching 119, 119 map entries (118 app/, 1 components/), 103 contextualized, 16 allowlisted. No lib/** entry exists, so PF2's two service modules need none.

CORRESPONDENCE_SCAN_ROOTS is lib/pipeline, lib/projects/service.ts, lib/portfolios/service.ts and lib/admin — both PF2 service modules are ALREADY covered, app/** is not. CONTENT_MODIFYING_SITES carries 15 entries, all naming lib/pipeline modules. The correspondence rule and the >50 vocabulary floor are as the parent described.

Four existing test cases across two describe blocks, carrying five expect() calls: create allows authorized roles, create rejects unauthorized roles, create fails validation without a name, and the readiness statistic is labelled LEGACY_NON_AUTHORITATIVE. PF2 extends this file; it may not weaken or delete any of these. The second of them currently passes against an analyst-admitting array and must keep passing against canManagePortfolio, which excludes analyst.
One describe block per helper, each with an allow case and a deny case. PF2 adds the canManagePortfolio block in the same shape.

Post-PF1. aggregatePortfolioSroi(projects: ProjectRunSummary[]) accepts any array; getPortfolioAnalytics(portfolioId: string) accepts the id only. The aggregate-coverage invariant rests on call sites, not on types.

portfolios carries status varchar default 'active' with status_check IN ('active','archived') at :138; projects carries portfolio_id as a nullable FK at :183 with idx_projects_portfolio_id at :218. Both match the parent's citations exactly. No schema change is needed and none is authorized.

MEASURED_BASELINE_OF_THE_IMPLEMENTATION_.implication: PF2 is a from-scratch build of the composition surface, not a correction of one: five of the six frozen behaviours have no implementation at all at AS_OF_TREE, the sixth (create) carries two defects the parent's decisions correct, and no UPDATE of projects.portfolio_id exists anywhere in the tree.

OPEN_FINDINGS.title: PF2's frozen new server-action module moves an exact pin that lives outside PF2's authorized write surface.
OPEN_FINDINGS.detail: tests/database-runtime-entrypoints.test.ts:775 asserts { inventoried: 141, reaching: 116, contextualized: 100, allowlisted: 16 } over the regex layer's app/** entry points. ENTRY_POINT_PATTERNS at :172-192 includes /^actions\.tsx?$/, so app/app/portfolios/[portfolioId]/actions.ts — which the parent freezes in PF2's surface — is an entry point, and creating it moves the quadruple to { 142, 117, 101, 16 }. The parent's PF2 path set contains tests/database-entrypoint-inventory.json (the AST layer's data file) but NOT tests/database-runtime-entrypoints.test.ts (the regex layer's assertion). The parent artifact, the batch manifest and the PF1 authority each contain ZERO occurrences of the string 'database-runtime-entrypoints'.
OPEN_FINDINGS.why_non_blocking: It blocks the IMPLEMENTATION node, not this authority-only mission. It is fully measured, it has a named release condition, and it is disclosed rather than resolved by silently widening a frozen parent enumeration — which would be exactly the authority expansion the operating rules forbid.
OPEN_FINDINGS.disposition: Recorded as LOCKS.LOCK_ENTRYPOINT_REGEX_LAYER_PIN, with its release condition and an explicit list of what may NOT be done instead. Neither parent artifact is edited and PF2's write surface is not widened.

OPEN_FINDINGS.title: The 'application and database both refuse' guarantee holds on the organization axis and has no counterpart on the role axis.
OPEN_FINDINGS.detail: The parent's composition_contract.same_org_validation states that composition is enforced by the application and additionally by RLS, naming projects_update_allowed_roles and portfolios_*. Measured, both policies (db/migrations/0031_rls_core.sql:231-241 and :265-275, reproduced in db/baseline/stella_g2_schema.sql:9366 and db/policies/001_initial_auth_rls.sql:265) admit 'analyst' in USING and WITH CHECK. The analyst exclusion adjudicated in permissions.analyst_adjudication is therefore enforced by canManagePortfolio alone.
OPEN_FINDINGS.why_non_blocking: The parent's sentence is scoped to same-ORGANIZATION validation and is exact within that scope; the gap is a silence about the role axis, not a false statement. Nothing needs to change in the database: FIBC-038 is NO_DB_OBJECT and closing it would require a migration the parent forbids.
OPEN_FINDINGS.disposition: Frozen as ROLE_ENFORCEMENT_LAYER and pinned by PF2-NEG-ROLE-RLS-1 and PF2-MUT-ROLE-RLS-1, so that a PF2 implementer cannot write a PostgreSQL control asserting an analyst denial that the database will not deliver, and cannot record a green RLS run as evidence of the narrowing.

OPEN_FINDINGS.title: The live create path can produce an archived portfolio with no portfolio.archived audit row.
OPEN_FINDINGS.detail: PortfolioInputSchema (lib/portfolios/service.ts:11-15) declares status as z.enum(['active','archived']).default('active') and createPortfolioForCurrentOrganization writes data.status straight into the insert at :54. db/schema.ts:138's status_check admits both values and constrains no transition. The shipped form does not supply status, so the defect is unreachable from the UI today and reachable from the exported service function.
OPEN_FINDINGS.why_non_blocking: PF2's create and update contracts close it as a consequence of implementing this authority, and it is recorded because it is a distinct defect from the inline-role-array defect and an auditor should see both named.
OPEN_FINDINGS.disposition: Closed by STATUS_INPUT_CONTRACT when PF2 is implemented, pinned by PF2-NEG-STATUS-1, PF2-NEG-UNARCHIVE-1 and PF2-MUT-STATUS-1.

OPEN_FINDINGS.title: One concurrent lane is open against a Portfolio shared writer at AS_OF_TREE.
OPEN_FINDINGS.detail: PR #105 (open, draft, base integration/commercial-v1) changes lib/audit/logger.ts, one of the three shared-writer files the parent assigns to PF2 for the Portfolio lane. Its two appended verbs are three-segment values, which the two-segment shape pin at lib/audit/__tests__/logger.test.ts:34 does not admit; PF2's five verbs are two-segment and satisfy that pin unchanged.
OPEN_FINDINGS.why_non_blocking: The parent already anticipated ordinary concurrency on these three files and prescribes the resolution — synchronise before editing, re-apply rather than overwrite. This finding supplies the measured identity of the concurrent lane at AS_OF_TREE and the measured proof that PF2 does not share its defect class.
OPEN_FINDINGS.disposition: Recorded as LOCKS.LOCK_AUDIT_ACTION_VOCABULARY with an explicit release condition.

OPEN_FINDINGS.title: app/app/portfolios/[portfolioId]/page.tsx is authorized to two different nodes with no serialization rule.
OPEN_FINDINGS.detail: The parent lists that path in BOTH authorized_future_implementation_surface.PF2_composition_and_permissions and .PF3_comparison_health_and_intelligence. shared_writer_serialization names only lib/audit/logger.ts, tests/database-entrypoint-inventory.json and tests/audit-action-contract.test.ts, so the one file two Portfolio nodes are both authorized to write is the one file the serialization rule does not cover.
OPEN_FINDINGS.why_non_blocking: PF3 is not authorized and has no successor artifact, so no concurrent Portfolio writer exists at AS_OF_TREE. The exposure begins only when a PF3 execution authority is materialized.
OPEN_FINDINGS.disposition: Disclosed here so that the PF3 successor addresses it rather than discovering it as a conflict. This authority does not resolve it and does not edit the parent; PF2's own obligation is unchanged.

READY_FOR_PF2_IMPLEMENTATION: NO — an independent Opus exact-object audit of this artifact, followed by integration into integration/commercial-v1, followed by the release of LOCK-AUDIT-ACTION-VOCABULARY and LOCK-ENTRYPOINT-REGEX-LAYER-PIN, are all required first.
